target.title: fix #95295: [Bug]: Web UI sidebar hides existing child-spawned subagent sessions across agent scopes
target.body:
Fixes #95295.

## What Problem This Solves

- **Affected surface / workflow:** Control UI sidebar session discovery across configured agent scopes.
- **Root cause, in product terms:** The default sidebar request is intentionally scoped to the selected agent, and the sidebar projection independently removes subagent-keyed and `spawnedBy` rows. The prior opt-in implementation widened both layers through shared session state, so a later scoped chat refresh could replace the all-agent rows while the **All agents** button remained pressed.
- **Why it matters / User impact:** Persisted child-spawned work could exist in another agent store but remain undiscoverable from the sidebar, and the previous toggle could visibly claim an all-agent view while showing only one agent's sessions.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Fix classification:** Root-cause repair.
- **Complete shipped solution:** The default sidebar remains scoped. Pressing **All agents** performs the existing unscoped `sessions.list({})` request into sidebar-owned state, enables child/spawned rows only for that local result, and leaves shared canonical scoped state untouched. Canonical list revisions and session-created events coalesce background refreshes of the local result; stale responses, disconnects, gateway-client replacement, and session-capability replacement cannot reactivate old rows.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The sidebar now owns both sides of the opt-in invariant: its unscoped data source and its child-row projection. A scoped refresh can continue publishing canonical state without contradicting the pressed control, and disabling the control immediately returns to the latest canonical scoped result.
- **Key design boundary / source of truth:** The existing `sessions.list` contract and combined session-store loader remain authoritative. Omitting `agentId` is already the canonical all-agent read; this patch does not add a protocol, schema, config, persistence, or migration contract.
- **Non-goals / what did not change:** The Sessions page, command palette, primary-session selection, chat picker, default scoped visibility, gateway protocol/schema, persisted transcript format, and session migration behavior are unchanged.
- **Compatibility, merge-risk, or maintainer-decision notes:** The behavior is default-off and sidebar-only. Maintainers should still confirm that opt-in sidebar discovery of persisted child transcripts across configured agents is the intended product boundary.
- **Risk labels considered:** `merge-risk: session-state`, visibility boundary, compatibility, and performance.
- **Risk explanation:** The opt-in mode can reveal persisted child/subagent transcripts from other configured agent scopes and performs a bounded all-agent list read. It does not mutate shared canonical state or stored sessions.
- **Why acceptable:** The wider visibility is explicit and user initiated; archived, global, unknown, and cron rows remain excluded; the existing list limit/configured-agent behavior remains in force; and default behavior is unchanged.
- **Patch quality notes:** Production changes are confined to sidebar state/rendering, the existing navigation projection, and the scope-control style. The additional E2E change is the requested visible-browser regression. No suppression directives, skipped tests, lockfile changes, protocol changes, or unrelated refactors were added.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High for contributor-side correctness and the current-main port; final cross-agent transcript visibility scope remains an explicit maintainer product decision.

## User Impact

- **Users/operators/developers can now:** Enable **All agents** in the sidebar and rediscover an existing cross-agent child-spawned session, while newly created sessions and canonical list revisions refresh that opt-in view.
- **Existing behavior preserved:** With the control off, the sidebar remains agent-scoped and continues hiding subagent-keyed and `spawnedBy` rows. Scoped chat/session refreshes continue publishing their normal canonical result.
- **What was not tested or remains unavailable:** This repair did not rerun a long-lived provider-backed gateway with real user transcripts. The PR already has reviewer-viewable gateway/store/browser proof and carries `proof: sufficient`; the fresh repair adds a current-main Chromium mocked-Gateway E2E and captured local screenshot rather than claiming a new live-provider run.

## Evidence

- **Environment:** Windows Git Bash, Node `v22.17.0`, pnpm `11.2.2`, repository Playwright Chromium, current `origin/main`. pnpm reported the repository's preferred Node floor (`>=22.19.0`) as a non-fatal warning.
- **Commands run after this patch:**
  - `pnpm test ui/src/lib/sessions/navigation.test.ts ui/src/components/app-sidebar.test.ts`
  - `OPENCLAW_CAPTURE_UI_PROOF=1 pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts ui/src/e2e/session-management.e2e.test.ts`
  - `pnpm tsgo:test:ui`
  - `pnpm ui:i18n:check`
  - `pnpm ui:build`
  - `pnpm exec oxfmt --check ui/src/components/app-sidebar.ts ui/src/components/app-sidebar.test.ts ui/src/lib/sessions/navigation.ts ui/src/lib/sessions/navigation.test.ts ui/src/styles/layout.css ui/src/e2e/session-management.e2e.test.ts`
  - `git diff --check`
- **Key results / observations:** Focused UI tests passed 2 files / 23 tests. The Chromium E2E passed 1 file / 10 tests; its new scenario locates scoped `Main`, verifies the cross-agent child is absent, presses **All agents**, locates `Subagent: Planner`, verifies `aria-pressed="true"`, and verifies the final `sessions.list` request omits `agentId`. UI test type-check, all 20 locale checks, production Control UI build, formatting, and diff whitespace checks passed. Public existing proof: [Real behavior proof run 29063489211 / job 86270110876](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29063489211/job/86270110876); the PR carries `proof: sufficient`. A full repository type-check attempt encountered an unrelated current-main `TS4058` in `src/secrets/config-io.ts`; this PR does not modify that file, and the requested UI type-check passes.
- **Review findings addressed, if any:** RF-001 contributor work is addressed by the current-main port and fresh requested validation. RF-002, RF-003, and RF-006 are fixed by sidebar-owned all-agent data and tested scoped-refresh isolation. RF-004 and RF-005 are addressed by the focused current-main port. RF-007 passed with 23 focused tests. RF-008 passed with 10 Chromium E2E tests including the cross-agent child reveal. RF-009 passed (`pnpm tsgo:test:ui`). RF-010 passed (`pnpm ui:i18n:check`, all locales clean). RF-011 passed (`git diff --check`). Product acceptance of the default-off visibility boundary remains a maintainer decision.
- **Regression guardrail:** Navigation tests lock down scoped/default filtering and all-agent exclusions; component tests lock down local request ownership, scoped-refresh isolation, revision/created-event refreshes, in-flight coalescing, stale-response rejection, lifecycle resets, and failure fallback; the Chromium E2E locks down the rendered control, visible child locator, and omitted `agentId` request.
